en:Console:b1d65c8343.text: Everything that exists at developers.banzami.com, screen by screen — and what each thing means before you use it.

en:Console:243e135e99.text: Four things, nested inside one another. Worth reading once, because nearly every integration mistake is one of these four mistaken for another.

en:Console:3362b7f491.text: Person ≠ Workspace. A person belongs to several workspaces; a workspace has several members.

en:Console:11513d2750.text: Workspace ≠ Project. The workspace is the access boundary. The project is the integration boundary: keys, webhooks and logs belong to the project.

en:Console:e00dcba7f5.text: Project ≠ Business. The project is your application. The Business is the legal entity that receives the money. Financial Setup connects them, and a project with

en:Console:309c790f31.text: Business ≠ wallet account. The Business has a wallet; the wallet has segregated accounts. Accounts are where value separates by campaign, store or event.

en:Console:92309d72ed.text: Authority flows down, never up. Your key identifies the Project; the Project determines the Business; the Business determines the wallet and its accounts. No fi

en:Console:d51b3884c3.text: Your personal profile, at /conta. You sign in with an email and a six-digit code: there is no password to choose, forget or reuse.

en:Console:d4dd84cad9.text: Profile — the name people who share a workspace with you see. The email is your identifier and is not editable.

en:Console:cd5650e4f5.text: Security — describes the real model: a code by email, a session in a cookie. There are no password or MFA controls because neither exists.

en:Console:c7efeb2b6f.text: Sessions — your open sessions, with origin and last use, and a button to end all the others. This is the screen for the day you lose a laptop.

en:Console:1a7d36cea0.text: Sign out — asks for confirmation. Cancel keeps the session; confirming ends it, and the browser back button does not bring it back.

en:Console:0ab023be4e.text: A workspace is who has access. Creating one is immediate and involves nobody at Banzami.

en:Console:e15c2f6cd6.text: Inviting produces a link the Console copies for you. Whoever accepts it signs in with their own email and their own code — the invitation names the role, not th

en:Console:2d9c40b4f4.text: Leaving a workspace is always possible, except for the last Owner: a workspace is never left without one.

en:Console:5a93da9b45.text: Transferring ownership takes two steps: an Owner gives the Owner role to another member and then leaves or changes their own role. There is no single button tha

en:Console:2c0194b9ac.text: Archiving a workspace is refused while it still has active projects, and the refusal says how many. Archive those first.

en:Console:1c92055f54.text: Deleting is only possible when the workspace is genuinely empty. A workspace with history is archived; one that never held anything disappears.

en:Console:3cf5ffcf21.text: Under Settings · Activity, the workspace's administrative record: who changed what, to whom, and when. Invitations, joins and departures, role changes and remov

en:Console:11cfac27b9.text: This workspace and no other. The record is filtered by the workspace you are already a member of; there is no way to ask for somebody else's.

en:Console:8b818007b5.text: Owners and Admins. Seeing who has access and who granted it is a management question, and those are the roles that can change it too.

en:Console:294a24b61f.text: It is nobody's account security history. Personal sessions, sign-in codes and account settings are not here — they live under /conta, and belong to that person

en:Console:f55e736c54.text: No secrets. A key that was created appears as an event; its value, its prefix and webhook secrets appear nowhere.

en:Console:9386fbfd39.text: Permanent. It cannot be edited or deleted from the Console, and it outlives what it describes: a deleted project still appears here.

en:Console:5805f3cc4a.text: Activity is not Logs. Activity answers "who has authority here, and who gave it to them" — workspace administration. Logs answers "what did my application ask t

en:Console:0e15524482.text: The project is the unit of integration: one application, one set of keys, its webhooks and its logs. One application, one project.

en:Console:1a2af1ed70.text: The Project ID does not change. Renaming changes the label and nothing else — the id you wrote into your configuration stays valid.

en:Console:fa144eee78.text: Deleting is possible while the project has no history at all: no key ever issued, no request logged, no financial connection. The Console says what is in the wa

en:Console:b5f2b15dbb.text: Archiving is what you do to a project that had history. Archiving revokes the active keys and says how many — and from then on a call with any of them answers 4

en:Console:130606565f.text: An archived project leaves the selector and returns behind “Show archived”, marked as archived.

en:Console:fdf4d1718f.text: This is where a project gains a financial owner. Without it everything works — keys, webhooks, integration — except receiving money. That split is deliberate: y

en:Console:8c0b9b5e3e.text: A new Business. You submit an application — entity, representative, documents — and Banzami verifies it. It is a human decision, and it takes as long as it take

en:Console:90169b5062.text: An existing Business. If the entity is already verified with Banzami, its owner issues you a consent code. Paste it, and the project connects to that Business w

en:Console:9796671999.text: The fee is not yours to choose. Banzami assigns pricing to the Business; no field in your request selects it, and no path through the Console changes it.

en:Console:1b643ca6c8.text: The name is yours: it tells the key apart in the list and in Workspace activity, and changes nothing about what it can do.

en:Console:43d7903f14.text: Scopes are chosen at creation and do not change. A read-only key will never write.

en:Console:d65a29305c.text: The secret appears exactly once, in the creation dialog, with a copy button. After that the list shows the prefix and a mask.

en:Console:71d9d07a84.text: Where to keep the key and what never to do with it is in Security.

en:Console:3a481613bd.text: Registering an HTTPS endpoint returns the signing secret exactly once.

en:Console:8a66095d05.text: Redelivering repeats the same delivery — it is that delivery again, not a new one.

en:Console:1622fdee89.text: Owner | Everything, including inviting, changing roles, archiving and deleting. The last owner cannot leave — there is no workspace without one.
